data.G: At assembly, compare only research candidates that pass the full correctness checks. Try measured combinations where useful, but evaluate each integrated program independently; do not assume the gains add. Select by the official geometric-mean objective, then use the controller’s independent confirmation before finalizing. Preserve the required kernel ABI, AoS layout, launch.json schema, and single-kernel interface.
data.analysis: Choose N=4 for four complementary hypotheses: source-data reuse, parallelizing the serial per-target reduction, launch geometry, and per-interaction arithmetic. The supplied kernel computes all N² interactions with one thread per target. The baseline launch maps each CTA to 256 targets, yielding only 16, 32, and 64 CTAs at the three official sizes; this makes smaller CTAs worth measuring, but does not prove an occupancy bottleneck. The valid, correct baseline reports three timing repeats averaging 0.0018526411283622502 seconds; no per-size breakdown or profile is provided, so the cost hypotheses remain unverified. The frozen target is one GH200 with NVRTC CUDA 12.6.3. ROMEO documents GH200 GPUs on AArch64 nodes; CUDA 12.6.3 Best Practices Guide discusses shared-memory reuse and explicit rsqrtf use. All candidates must retain the specified behavior and pass correctness before timing comparisons.

children.objective: In src/nbody_kernel.cu, retain one thread per target and the existing force arithmetic while cooperatively staging source x, y, z, and mass tiles in shared memory for reuse across the CTA’s targets. Handle partial source tiles and target tails safely, retain self-interaction exclusion, and keep shared memory within the 49,152-byte limit. Sweep feasible tile sizes and matching block/items_per_block settings; use only the permitted source and launch files. Judge candidates by full correctness and the official per-size geometric-mean timing protocol.
children.subject: CTA-level shared-memory reuse of source-particle fields

children.objective: Explore a warp-cooperative traversal in which each warp owns one target and its lanes accumulate disjoint source-particle subsets, then reduce the three force components within the warp; one lane writes the complete output state. For this mapping, make items_per_block equal the number of target warps per CTA (block/32), and handle N tails, self pairs, coincident positions, and all output fields correctly. Keep this path distinct from shared-memory tiling and measure only candidates passing all correctness checks.
children.subject: Warp-parallel inner-loop reduction per target

children.objective: Keep the one-thread-per-target traversal, force equations, and memory strategy unchanged; isolate launch-geometry effects by comparing legal block sizes with items_per_block equal to block and shared_memory_bytes zero. In particular, test whether smaller CTAs improve the measured workload without assuming that more CTAs guarantee a gain. Preserve the exact JSON key set and validate every supported size before comparing official timings.
children.subject: Launch-geometry tuning for the baseline ownership mapping

children.objective: Keep the one-thread-per-target and source traversal structure while exploring algebraically equivalent interaction arithmetic, such as explicit rsqrtf-based inverse-distance-cubed scaling and cancellation of the target-mass multiply/divide. Preserve float32 softening, self-pair handling, velocity-then-position update order, and exact mass copying. Do not enable global fast math; validate numerical tolerances, nonfinite-output checks, and the extreme-mass case before judging timing.
children.subject: Per-interaction arithmetic throughput with correctness-bounded transforms
